objective: Take up SHARED-CONTACT-20261108-001's selected next step (G5 with G1, the contact-network gate read across time): three rings in a chain, A, B and C, ring B sharing one contact cell with A and another with C. Prove that listening contacts never compose (a contact that feeds nothing back cannot carry one ring's past to another contact), bound when the far contact can first depend on the far ring, and give the linear criterion; then measure, exactly at every lag where the dynamics repeats within a cap, how often both contacts persist and how often the far contact binds the two end rings through the middle ring, and whether the second follows from the first.
status: Complete 2026-11-08: listening contacts never compose; in a shared chain the far ring reaches the far contact only from lag d + 1; of 5,632 chains of three rings both contacts persist in 182 and none of them binds its end rings at every lag from d + 1 on (one size past with off-centre contacts, the same); post hoc, 195 chains bind their ends at recurring lags (154 with both contacts binding there), never with both contacts persistent. Recommendation: Research directions (intermittent networks, A34; a middle ring that carries without mixing).
stop_rule: Stop when the listening, light-cone and linear statements are proved and the chain census is done on the declared rings, with the composition hypothesis decided on it, or an obstruction is found and explained.
title: Two contacts across time: persistent contacts do not compose
